scope: Counter-based Gaussian values, a three-compartment epidemic SDE ensemble with an input-replacement world and a component-hold world, the exact mean and variance of a square-root diffusion with a piecewise-constant input, and the dense Euler quasi log likelihood of numpy-drawn trajectories.
independence_basis: Coefficients are written out in NumPy rather than evaluated through the expression tape; the quasi-likelihood data come from numpy.random.default_rng. The reference imports no Antecedent code. The ensemble moments replay a documented algorithm (SplitMix64 counter generator, Euler-Maruyama with shared half-step Brownian paths) and so share that specification with the product; the square-root diffusion moments are closed-form ODE solutions that need no noise realization.
historical_exposure: Written by the repository author alongside the product; whether the product source was consulted is unrecorded.
limitations: The reference is a NumPy reimplementation by the repository author of the same documented algorithm, so the epidemic ensemble moments, the counter-based generator and the Euler likelihood agree because both implement one specification; they do not validate that specification against an external SDE package. Independence of the square-root diffusion moments (exact ODEs) and of the numpy.random.default_rng trajectories is stronger. The Rust ensemble assertions compare grids at 1e-8 * (1 + |expected|) and the likelihood at relative 1e-9; the reference check itself compares at rtol and atol 1e-9. One epidemic parameter set and 200 paths; Monte Carlo moments are replays, not coverage or calibration.
redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. Python standard library only, in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.
